headline: MGAT Alpha closed 11 trades this week for a net +$564.41 (54.55% win rate) — the best headline week of the run, and for the first time the book is running ahead of simply holding its starting coin basket (+7.10% versus the basket's +2.04%). The result is heavily concentrated: one position held for two hours produced 91% of the week's profit and 64% of the run's entire cumulative gain, priced by a single source with no independent check against it. Excluding that one trade the week was a modest +$48.58 and the book remains behind the hold benchmark, where it has sat every week since launch, while three of the four position families lost money this week even as the headline improved.

counterfactual.reason: The shadow comparison book could never close a position, so none of its figures measure anything.

hold_benchmark.basis: $8,000 split equally across the seven coins the book bought in its first two cycles on 2026-08-25, held untouched, no fees

llm_adviser: LLM adviser: observer only — logs what it would do, cannot affect a trade (settled from source 2026-09-22).
sample_caveat: 11 closed trades this week, 69 all-time against the 200-trade target — about 35% of the way to a sample worth treating as meaningful. The all-time count is past the point where win rate and PnL move from purely directional to readable, but this week two trades on one coin produced 91% of the week's profit and 64% of the run's entire cumulative profit, so the headline numbers are not yet a measurement of the strategy — they are effectively two records plus noise.
paper_caveat: Alpha is paper — simulated fills, no slippage, no thin-liquidity exits, no can't-sell-into-dust. A clean logic result here is never a claim that the execution floor works; that claim belongs to the Beta rung alone.
integrity: No entries in the repair ledger fall within this week's window, so the comparison with the prior week is clean.

verdict.text: Needs a change — and the change is to how prices get verified, not to the trading logic itself. The headline is the best of the run and the first time the book has out-run its hold benchmark, but neither holds up once one position is set aside: remove the two-hour trade that produced 91% of this week's profit and the book is roughly +0.66% against a benchmark of +2.04%, which is close to where it has sat every week since launch. That one position, together with a second one from three weeks ago on the same coin, account for about 64% of the run's entire cumulative profit, and both were priced by a single source with no independent reference to check them against — the pipeline could not have caught a bad print either way. A separate price check also flagged one closed position's exit price as nearly six times different from an independent reference this week, the first flag of that size on a coin outside the run's one known false-alarm case. Set against that: the all-time win rate improved, the trades priced on a verified, independently-measured basis were modestly profitable for a second straight week, and no critical system faults fired. Three of the four position families lost money this week on small samples, which supports no conclusion either way about the trading logic — the open question this week is the price pipeline, not the strategy.
